events.title: Charlemagne convenes an assembly in Rome to judge Pope Leo III
events.description: A week after arriving in Rome, Charlemagne called an assembly in St Peter's to hear charges against Pope Leo III, who cleared himself by oath. On Christmas Day Leo crowned Charlemagne emperor.
events.html: A week after arriving in Rome, Charlemagne called an assembly in St Peter's to hear charges against Pope Leo III, who cleared himself by oath. On Christmas Day Leo crowned Charlemagne emperor.

events.title: Henry V enters Paris in triumph
events.description: Henry V of England rode into Paris alongside Charles VI of France. Under the Treaty of Troyes he was regent and heir to the French throne, but his death in 1422 left the dual monarchy to his infant son.
events.html: Henry V of England rode into Paris alongside Charles VI of France. Under the Treaty of Troyes he was regent and heir to the French throne, but his death in 1422 left the dual monarchy to his infant son.

events.title: Portuguese conspirators end Spanish rule in Lisbon
events.description: Nobles stormed the royal palace in Lisbon and proclaimed the Duke of Braganza king as John IV. The coup ended 60 years of union with Spain; the Braganza dynasty reigned until 1910.

events.title: Juan Lavalle overthrows Governor Manuel Dorrego in Buenos Aires
events.description: Returning with troops who had fought in the Cisplatine War, Juan Lavalle of the Unitarian Party mounted a coup in Buenos Aires Province, deposing Governor Manuel Dorrego, whom he captured and killed. The coup reignited the Argentine Civil Wars.

events.title: Ford installs a moving assembly line for the whole car
events.description: At Highland Park, Michigan, Ford began building the Model T on a moving assembly line. Assembly time fell from over 12 hours to about 90 minutes, and cheap cars reshaped modern industry.

events.title: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat
events.description: Rosa Parks was arrested in Montgomery, Alabama, for refusing to give her seat to a white passenger. The 381-day bus boycott that followed brought Martin Luther King Jr. to national prominence.

events.title: Twelve nations sign the Antarctic Treaty
events.description: In Washington, twelve countries, including the United States and the Soviet Union, agreed to reserve Antarctica for peaceful scientific research. The treaty banned military activity and froze territorial claims.

events.title: Tunnellers from Britain and France meet under the Channel
events.description: British and French workers broke through the last wall of rock and shook hands beneath the English Channel. The tunnel opened in 1994, linking Britain to the Continent by rail.

intl.name: World AIDS Day
intl.description: The first ever global health day when it launched in 1988, World AIDS Day calls on individuals, communities, and governments to unite in the fight against HIV, remember those who have died, and support the more than 38 million people living with the virus.
